reason: The cited evidence shows that trace interstitials promote phase segregation and α-Ti precipitate formation during 700°C aging, but it reports softening, not brittle fracture or toughness loss, and the precipitates are not described as brittle intermetallic/Laves phases that interrupt dislocation motion. The key premises about brittle fracture and toughness reduction are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Trace interstitials (O, N) induce local compositional segregation during aging
Segregation triggers nucleation of brittle secondary phases (e.g., intermetallic, Laves-type)
Brittle phases interrupt dislocation motion and plastic deformation mechanisms
This reduces toughness and promotes brittle fracture under mechanical loading
Aging at 700°C in ambient atmosphere will incorporate impurities and cause these effects
